question: In Surah Al-'Asr (103:1-3), Allah swears by 'Time'. What does this emphasize for a believer?
options: That time is an irreplaceable trust and human life slips away unless filled with faith, good deeds, and patience
That only scholarly time counts towards salvation
That worldly work is completely prohibited
explanation: Imam Ash-Shafi'i famously remarked that if humanity only reflected on Surah Al-'Asr, it would be sufficient guidance for organizing their lives and prioritizing what truly matters.

question: What is the primary spiritual antidote taught in the Qur'an for a restless, agitated heart (Surah Ar-Ra'd 13:28)?
options: Endless news and social media monitoring
The sincere remembrance of Allah (Dhikr)
Total isolation from society
explanation: Allah states: 'Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah hearts are assured.' When digital dopamine leaves the heart feeling empty and dry, Dhikr returns peace and tranquility.

question: The Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) said: 'Take benefit of five before five...' What are the two that directly relate to digital distraction?
options: Your wealth before poverty, and your fame before obscurity
Your youth before old age, and your free time before you become preoccupied
Your strength before sleep, and your meals before fasting
explanation: Narrated by Ibn Abbas (Al-Hakim, Sahih according to Al-Albani in Sahih al-Jami' 1077). Youth and free time are two of the greatest gifts that doom-scrolling quietly steals without the student noticing.

question: When observing blessings given to others online and feeling envy or FOMO, what does Islam encourage us to do?
options: Say 'Allahumma Barik' (May Allah bless them) and ask Allah from His infinite bounty
Compete to post a grander version of our own life
Criticize them in group chats
explanation: The Prophet (ﷺ) taught that praying for blessing (Barakah) for our brother removes envy from our own chest and invites angels to make the same dua for us.

question: The Prophet (ﷺ) described two blessings that many people are cheated out of (lose track of). What are they?
options: Health and free time (Sahih al-Bukhari 6412)
Gold and silver
Sleep and food
explanation: In Sahih al-Bukhari, Ibn Abbas reported that the Messenger of Allah said: 'There are two blessings in which many people are deceived: health and free time.' Mindful students guard both.

question: What is the Islamic etiquette when an unverified rumor or sensational claim appears on your social feed?
options: Immediately forward it to all groups to alert others
Verify the truth carefully before speaking or sharing (Surah Al-Hujurat 49:6)
Engage in public arguments in the comment section
explanation: Surah Al-Hujurat (49:6) commands believers: 'If there comes to you a disobedient one with information, investigate, lest you harm a people out of ignorance.' Verifying protects peace.

question: Why did the Prophet (ﷺ) teach Ali and Fatima (may Allah be pleased with them) the 33 SubhanAllah, 33 Alhamdulillah, and 34 Allahu Akbar tasbih before sleep?
options: As a physical and spiritual renewal greater than a domestic helper (Sahih al-Bukhari 3705)
As an alternative to obligatory prayers
Only for travelers on a journey
explanation: When Fatima was exhausted from household labor, the Prophet taught them this dhikr, stating it is better for their energy and peace of mind than having a servant.

question: What does Islam teach regarding excessive, idle speech and gossip (Laghw)?
options: Believers turn away with dignity and protect their focus (Surah Al-Mu'minun 23:3)
It is recommended for killing time
It is harmless as long as it is done online
explanation: Surah Al-Mu'minun describes the successful believers as 'those who turn away from ill speech / vanity.' Endless comment fights and drama fall directly into Laghw.

question: What happens when a person seeks forgiveness through Istighfar during moments of stress?
options: Allah opens a way out from every distress and relief from every anxiety (Sunan Abi Dawud 1518)
It causes more anxiety
It has no connection to mental well-being
explanation: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Whoever constantly seeks forgiveness, Allah will appoint for him a way out of every distress and a relief from every anxiety.'

question: What is the Sunnah attitude toward daily self-reflection (Muhasabah)?
options: Self-blame that leads to despair and giving up
Calm, honest reflection: taking account of oneself today before the ultimate account (Umar ibn al-Khattab)
Ignoring all mistakes completely
explanation: Umar (RA) advised: 'Hold yourselves to account before you are held to account.' Unscroll's Reflect tab embodies this calm, forgiving self-awareness without despair.
